title: App Container Can't Reach the Database Container
intro: You started both your app and database containers with plain 'docker run' (no Compose). The app logs are full of 'could not connect to database' errors.

steps.prompt: Confirm both containers are actually running.
steps.fake_output:
CONTAINER ID   IMAGE      NAMES   STATUS
a1b2c3d4       myapp      web     Up 2 minutes
e5f6g7h8       postgres   db      Up 5 minutes
steps.hint: Both are Up — so this isn't a crash, it's a connectivity problem between two running things.

steps.prompt: Check which network the 'web' container is actually on.
steps.hint: Note the network name here, then check the other container's network next.

steps.prompt: Now check which network the 'db' container is on.
steps.hint: Compare this against 'web's network from the previous step — are they the same?

steps.prompt: They're on different networks ('bridge' vs 'app-net'), which is why 'web' can't resolve 'db' by name. Connect 'web' to the 'app-net' network too.
steps.hint: A running container can be attached to an additional network without restarting it.

resolution: The two containers were started separately with plain 'docker run' and no shared --network flag, so 'web' landed on the default bridge network while 'db' was on a custom 'app-net' network created earlier. Containers on different networks can't resolve each other by name (and often can't route to each other at all) even on the same host. Connecting 'web' to 'app-net' fixed it immediately without restarting either container. The longer-term fix is starting both with the same explicit --network flag (or switching to Compose, which creates and wires up a shared network automatically) so this can't happen again on the next deploy.
